answer: One concrete defense: make each agent forge its identity by bonding real capital into a staked deposit that can be slashed for misbehavior. Minting a new identity then costs money, not just a throwaway cipher key, so flooding the network with clones becomes uneconomic. Honest agents emit a steady work pulse that peers measure over time, and reputation plus rewards accrue only to stake-backed, consistently active identities, starving cheap sybils of the history they need to earn trust.
